tier_reason: Enricher (2026-10-12): no valid measurement behind the reported numbers. src/test_benchmark.py and src/metrics.py count an answer identical to the input assembly as a pass without running it; each per-input speedup is floored at 1.0 with failed, non-compiling and benchmark-failing cases scored 1.0 and print_results.py clamps the geometric mean at 1.0; the released scripts time against gcc -O0 output although the paper states -O3. Crippled-baseline and floored-metric precedent.

Enricher (2026-10-12): the headline 1.29x is not a stable measurement. result.txt at commits 8be9917 and a955014 shows libc 0.3486 s vs AVX-256 0.3464 s (a tie) from the same harness, Makefile, byte-identical assembly and Xeon before commit 7d431e0 recorded 0.3494 vs 0.2711; the AVX-512 row was measured on two different routines (1024-byte then 2048-byte blocks); the result commits built the harness with gcc -O0, not -O3; and the AVX routines overrun both buffers for any length that is not a non-zero multiple of the block size (stb-zip precedent for the measured code, hidden by the 512 MiB buffers).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Harness built with gcc at default -O0 at the result commits (Makefile sets no optimisation flag); NASM for the assembly routines
